manual_derivations.scope: Manual protocol proof under the frozen complete polynomial lists, in either affine rings or each stated homogeneous ring
steps: Write d_F:P->I and d_G:Q->K. If pi(u,v)=0 and (u,v) is in Z, both d_F(u) and d_G(v) are zero. Polynomial flat extension of the two side kernels therefore gives ker(pi)=U. The identity embeddings in Y are flat as well.

For w in I intersect K, choose full original-generator expressions w=d_F(u)=d_G(b). Then (u,-b) belongs to Z and maps to w. This proves surjectivity with witnesses. For every cross column (g_j e_i,-f_i e_j), pi gives f_i g_j; those products generate IK.

Consequently Z/(U+V_K) is isomorphic to (I intersect K)/IK. With Tmem=(pi(M)+IK)/IK, quotienting by the full M gives ((I intersect K)/IK)/Tmem. No injectivity of d2, H2 vanishing, Tor over the separator, or flatness of quotient modules is required.

Tensor 0->I->R->R/I->0 with R/K. R is free over itself, so its positive Tor term vanishes, I tensor R/K is I/IK, and the kernel of I/IK->R/K is (I intersect K)/IK. Symmetry over the commutative polynomial ring identifies this with the stated Tor_1^R(R/I,R/K).

For homogeneous lists, take homogeneous degree-D components of the witnesses. Every generator has its declared shift, and arbitrary witnesses can be decomposed into homogeneous components. All homogeneous monomial multiples up to D are therefore sufficient. No high-degree cancellation can contribute a new homogeneous degree-D vector in this graded calculation.

E is a graded submodule. Since the ring is standard graded, (R_+ Q)_D is the sum over every variable of its multiplication image of Q_(D-1). Thus the prescribed rank difference gives the minimal generator births at D, using Q_(-1)=0. This says nothing about births above 8 or affine saturation.

manual_derivations.label: B-disjoint
manual_derivations.manual_derivation: In k[x,y], x^2 u+y^2 v=0 implies y^2 divides u and x^2 divides v. Hence Z=R(y^2,-x^2), exactly the cross-Koszul span; U=M=0 and both quotients vanish. The tagged generator is born in shifted degree 4.

manual_derivations.label: C0-hiddenTor
manual_derivations.manual_derivation: In k[s,x,y], s*x*u+s*y*v=0 reduces by domain cancellation to x*u+y*v=0. Hence Z=R(y,-x), shifted degree 3. U=M=0 and V_K=s*Z, so Q_rel=Q_raw is R/(s)(-3). pi(y,-x)=s*x*y; I intersect K=(s*x*y), IK=(s^2*x*y). Removing the surviving class would fail this control.

manual_derivations.label: C1-membershipduplicate
manual_derivations.manual_derivation: For the two tagged copies of nonzero m=F_3(s), Z=R(1,-1), V_K=m*Z and M=Z. Thus Q_raw is R/(m), with the generator-list shift, and Q_rel=0. In the homogeneous arm m=s(s-h)(s-2h), with degree 3; the same argument applies. Pairwise product relations alone leave the duplicate and do not suffice.

manual_derivations.label: C2-C3-gradedcollision
manual_derivations.manual_derivation: The two homogeneous quotients are respectively R/(s)(-3) and R/(s-h)(-3). Both defining linear forms have degree one, so their graded dimensions and generator births agree, while their annihilator ideals differ in the fixed labelled ring. A coordinate change can relate the presentations but does not make their annihilator-labelled R-modules identical.

manual_derivations.label: W-bare-widthone
manual_derivations.manual_derivation: Successively substitute each triangular equation x_i=x_(i-1)^2, with x_0=t and x_ell=s. Modulo the left ideal, s=t^(2^ell), so the last relation becomes y-t^(2^(ell+1)). The triangular quotient is k[t,y] before that last relation, proving the endpoint elimination ideal is exactly generated by that polynomial. Its degrees on the stated lengths are 4,8,16,32. The inclusion k[s]->k[t] sending s to t^(2^ell) is injective, so the separator-only contraction does not encode the endpoint degree. Sparse two-monomial encoding has short binary exponents; no exponential sparse-byte bound follows. The separate field-equation ideal changes the object and cannot erase this bare control.

manual_derivations.label: P2-projection-analysis
manual_derivations.manual_derivation: With complete tagged membership list m, the unreduced core projection pr:Z->Z_J is surjective: for a with sum a_i H_i in J choose membership coefficients b with sum a_i H_i+sum b_j m_j=0. Its kernel is exactly M. Therefore the quotient comparison naturally involves Z_J/pr(E), or a separately defined reduced target, rather than a map from Z/E to unquotiented Z_J. The already-frozen finite normal module R^r/Z_J used for coefficient signatures is yet another object. The protocol must name these targets and any grading/filtration comparison explicitly.
